messages:
maria: Quick sync — polishing the Capacity editor before the next release. Main areas: min/max steppers, burst toggle copy + toast, GPU pool chooser keyboard behavior, SLO slider labels/aria. 30m design huddle? Figma: https://figma.com/redwood/capacity-editor

jake: Dev note — steppers currently allow 0. Backend rejects 0 for reserved pools. Need client validation + clear inline error.

anya: Rather than a toast, show inline helper under the stepper: 'Min must be ≥ 1 for reserved pools.' That keeps context. Also the burst control should read like an override: 'Burst capacity (temporary)'.

sam: Copy nit: Spell out duration in the UI — 'Burst (temporary, up to 15 min)'. Helps avoid surprise.

olivia: A11y: keyboard focus order in the pool selector is inconsistent — focus lands on tag chips then back to the dropdown. Suggest making the whole control one composite widget with arrow key navigation. Also SLO slider is missing aria-valuetext.

kevin: SLO slider labels 'Latency' / 'Cost' are ambiguous. Suggest left/right labels: 'Lower latency' (left) and 'Lower cost' (right), plus a visible numeric value and a tooltip that explains tradeoffs.

maria: Good call. Guardrails question: when user sets min > budget, should the modal suggest auto-adjust or force the user to increase budget? Thoughts on CTA language?

anya: Prefer dual choices: primary 'Auto-adjust to budget' and secondary 'Increase budget'. Show a one-line explanation: 'Auto-adjust will pick the nearest feasible min based on pool granularity.'

jake: From backend side, auto-adjust will round to pool granularity and available capacity. UI must show the adjusted value before confirming. Will return computed value in API.

sam: UX animation note — applying burst currently flashes layout. Let's use a subtle crossfade and show a toast: 'Burst applied to pool <PoolName> for 15m'. Keep toast short and persistent for ~6s.

olivia: For screen readers, toasts should use role='status' and be announced, but not steal focus. Also warning icon contrast is below 4.5:1 on the orange variant. Need a darker tone.

ux-bot: Accessibility checklist updated: https://internal.redwood/a11y-checklist — added items: aria-valuetext for SLO slider, composite widget pattern for pool selector, toast role=status, contrast >= 4.5. Marking this thread for follow-up.

maria: Final asks for updated mocks before the sync: 1) validation states for min/max steppers (error + helper), 2) new burst copy + toast mock, 3) pool picker keyboard pattern example, 4) SLO slider with left/right labels, numeric readout and aria. @jake can you confirm implementation approach? @kevin can you prototype tooltip text?

jake: I'll add frontend validation + API flag for suggested auto-adjust. ETA: next Friday for feature branch. Punting aria until olivia's a11y branch merges.

kevin: Draft tooltip copy: 'Balancing latency vs cost. Moving the slider right favors lower cost at the expense of potentially higher latency. Use evaluation tests to verify your workload.' Will refine and post a short variant for the mock.

anya: Micro copy change: on the capacity modal change primary button text from 'Save' to 'Apply changes' — less ambiguous when presets exist.

sam: :thumbsup: If no objections I'll update the Figma file and attach a short prototype of the burst toast.

olivia: I'll run an a11y pass after the figma update and verify keyboard/aria changes. Thanks all!

maria: :spiral_calendar: Scheduling a 20m sync tomorrow 10:30am to walk through final mocks. Agenda: quick run through the 4 asks, confirm tooltip text, and lock copy. Adding calendar invite now.
